plan.summary: FEAT-LIW Chunk B (Flow Dispatch + WA Direct Entry). Three deliverables: (1) TriggerWelcomeFlowJob real dispatch — replace Chunk A placeholder with CronSchedulerJob-pattern execution (FlowGraphV2.Build + synthetic session + FlowEngineV2.ExecuteAsync + EndSessionAsync); slug→flow_definition resolution via NEW AutomationRepository.GetFlowByNameAndTenantAsync (treats chatbot_flows.flow_name as the slug, no migration). (2) Backend internal endpoint POST /api/internal/leads/intake/wa-direct with X-Internal-Service-Token auth (reuse Zoho's InternalServices:SharedSecret config + SlowEquals constant-time comparison). LeadIntakeService.IntakeWaDirectAsync reuses Chunk A normalization helpers but bypasses consent checks (implied consent — user initiated WA contact, GDPR Recital 32 affirmative action), source_slug='wa-direct' hardcoded, source='whatsapp' (NEW: UpsertIntakeLeadAsync gains a source parameter — Chunk A 'landing' default preserved). deviations.summary: BackendIntakeClient retry path is inline (try/catch + Task.Delay) instead of Polly WaitAndRetryAsync as the plan called for.
deviations.reason: Polly is not in the InvektoServices dependency graph today; PROJECT_CONFIG escalation_rules require Q approval before adding a new package. verification_questions.question: Slug→flow_name resolution: chatbot_flows.flow_name treated as slug (no migration). Risk: tenant Dashboard 'Rename Flow' silently breaks welcome trigger. Mitigation today: documented Chunk C scope item ('flow rename UI must warn if slug is wired in tenant_landing_settings.welcome_flow_slug'). Mitigation runtime: GetFlowByNameAndTenantAsync returns null → INV-AT-069 warn + skip (no exception, no hard fail). Acceptable trade-off vs migration 022 ADD COLUMN slug + backfill?

Welcome flow execution context — TriggerWelcomeFlowJob runs detached from a real chat session (no inbound message, no chat_id). FlowEngineV2.ExecuteAsync signature accepts contactKey and leadPreferredLocale as optional params. We'll pass: contactKey=lead.phone (E.164 from leads table), leadPreferredLocale=null (locale resolution is welcome flow's own concern; TR default in absence). SessionStateV2.CurrentNodeId starts at graph.TriggerStart!.Id. Question: should TriggerStart node type be validated (e.g., must be 'welcome_trigger' or 'manual_trigger')? CronSchedulerJob validates 'schedule_trigger' — wa-direct/landing welcome may use any entry-node type tenant configured. Open: validate or trust tenant config?

BackendIntakeClient HTTP base URL — Backend runs on port 5000 in dev, behind NSSM service in prod. Automation's existing MainAppCallbackClient already speaks to Backend; same base URL config (Backend:BaseUrl or InternalServices:BackendBaseUrl) reuse. Question: introduce a NEW config key 'InternalServices:BackendBaseUrl' (clean separation) OR reuse existing MainAppCallback URL (less config sprawl)? Q's expected answer based on patterns: reuse — but plan to confirm.

wa-direct hook fires on EVERY inbound message, not just first. EnsureLeadForWaDirectAsync handles idempotency at DB layer (existence check returns isNew=false within window). But Automation→Backend HTTP overhead per message (~20-50ms intra-cluster) is unavoidable. Alternative: Automation pre-checks via a lightweight local DB query (lead_exists?) — violates microservice isolation (leads is Backend-owned table). Plan accepts the HTTP overhead per inbound; question: is sub-50ms latency added to chat reply path acceptable, or is a per-tenant cache (tenant_id+phone → lead_id, 5min TTL ConcurrentDictionary in AutomationOrchestrator) warranted in v1?

verdict.raw_text: Codex iter 3 verdict was FAIL (CQ6+CQ9+Q4 dup-window-on-created_at + CQ11 schema-not-in-diff). Q overrode after reviewing the escalation summary because: (1) the dup-window semantic mirrors Chunk A which Codex passed on iter 4; (2) Q's interview decision was explicit ('Aynı 30g dup window — same as Chunk A'); (3) re-engagement-via-window-expiry is documented design intent in arch/contracts/lead-intake.json (window-dışı submission = duplicate=false = welcome fires intentionally); (4) Codex CQ11 flipped from PASS (iter 1+2) to UNKNOWN (iter 3) on identical schema-citation evidence — reviewer instability, not a real schema gap. Force-PASS is therefore not a quality compromise but a recognition that Codex iter 3 misread the intentional re-engagement semantic as a bug.

verdict.escalation_resolved_by: Q FORCE PASS (option A, recognized Codex over-strictness against documented Q-approved design)
verdict.escalation_reason: DECISION_CONFLICT — iter 3 surfaced CQ6+CQ9+Q4 (same root cause): Codex objects to wa-direct duplicate-window check anchored on leads.created_at, suggesting last_submission_at/updated_at instead. But: (a) this is the IDENTICAL semantic Chunk A landing intake uses (LeadIntakeService.cs:185-187, `(now - upsert.PriorCreatedAt.Value) <= dupWindow`) and Codex passed Chunk A on iter 4; (b) Q's interview answer explicitly chose 'Aynı dup window' (same as Chunk A); (c) re-engagement after window expiry is the DOCUMENTED design intent in arch/contracts/lead-intake.json — outside-window submission counts as duplicate=false so welcome fires, treating the contact as re-engagement-worthy. Codex iter 3 is asking for a behavioural change that contradicts (a) the established Chunk A precedent it already approved, (b) Q's explicit plan-time decision, and (c) the intentional re-engagement semantic. CQ11 also flipped from PASS (iter 1/2) to UNKNOWN (iter 3) on the same schema-citation evidence — reviewer instability. Q decision required: (i) FORCE PASS (recognize Codex over-strictness against Q-approved design), (ii) refactor wa-direct to use last_submission_at + apply same change to Chunk A landing for consistency (~1-2 day scope creep, breaks paired-deploy timeline), or (iii) explicitly diverge wa-direct semantic from Chunk A and document why.
